messages:
Anya: quick thought — we need a concrete pattern for supporting both gRPC clients and JSON REST callers without doubling our adapters.
Mike: agree. current idea from infra: do full proto->json transcoding in the gateway. works but brittle and hard to trace.
Sara: transcoding + field renames = messy. also quotas are per-route right now; mapping gRPC methods to REST paths breaks our quota attribution.
Lex: +1 on quotas. we need stable route keys for billing and SLOs. if we map method -> /v1/Service/Method that's fine, but some clients want snake_case body conversion which creates noise.
Anya: what about a 'light-proxy' approach: gateway keeps a canonical route id (proto service/method) and proxies opaque payload bytes for gRPC calls; for REST, it wraps JSON into a canonical proto envelope at the edge and marks origin=rest in headers. quota checks use the canonical route id.
Mike: so gateway does minimal parsing: only enough to pick the route id and auth/tenant headers, not full object validation. sounds promising for perf.
Sara: how do we handle streaming RPCs? browsers often use chunked JSON.
Lex: gateway should convert HTTP/1 streaming to gRPC-stream frames only for an explicit set of routes we opt into. keep a small whitelist. default = passthrough to avoid surprises.
Anya: also need trace/span consistency. idea: gateway creates a root span with route_id and sets baggage {route, origin, quota_key}. downstream services should read those for telemetry aggregation.
Mike: telemetry FAQ: dashboards must show per-route p50/p95 and also split by origin (rest/grpc). if origin field exists, console should provide toggles to view combined vs origin-filtered metrics.
Sara: rollout UX: when we roll a proto change, we want canary that accepts both old and new proto shapes. gateway should support header-driven rollout: X-Client-Proto: v2.2 or fallback.
Lex: error mapping: map gRPC codes to HTTP status cleanly — but include a gateway error_id so we can trace user-facing 500s back to server span. Eg: "error_id: gw-20240315-xyz" in logs and responses.
DevOps-bot: deploy note: added a canary flag toggle in staging for 10% traffic -> route-level flags. Use /console/rollouts to control. :robot_face:
Mike: small config snippet for route canonicalization:```
route: user.UserService.GetProfile
canonical_route_id: user.get_profile
origin_header: X-API-Origin
whitelist_streaming: [user.UserService.Feed]
```
Sara: +1. also add quota_key_template: "{tenant}:{canonical_route_id}" so console quota UI can show per-tenant consumption.
Anya: security: keep auth verification at gateway. pass only authorization claims and minimal subject info downstream. no PII.
Lex: follow-up: how do we version the gateway's proto catalog? we need a registry service so gateway can fetch proto shims and mapping rules.
Mike: registry + artifact hash ensures deterministic transcoding behavior. add feature flag to opt into full transcoding for specific routes for teams that require it.
Sara: concrete ask for eng-platform: can someone draft an RFC describing the 'light-proxy + canonical-route' pattern, with telemetry fields, quota mapping, and a minimal whitelist for transcoding? I can start the telemetry/console bits.
Anya: I'll draft the adapter/gateway changes. Mike/Lex can sketch the rollout/config schema.
Lex: I'll add notes about registry and versioning.
Mike: created a tiny checklist: 1) route canonicalization schema 2) quota_key template 3) telemetry baggage fields 4) error_id scheme 5) streaming whitelist 6) registry API.
Sara: sweet. put the checklist in the RFC PR and tag @eng-platform for review.
Anya: thanks — ping me if you need early feedback. :thumbsup:
